name: gate3-alltoall-intra-node
description: All-to-all confined to 8 ranks (one node, XGMI). This is the EP=8 topology that the reference MoE configuration relies on, and the control case for every cross-node result.

gates.name: alltoall_passed
gates.note: Correctness, uneven splits and communicator churn all clean.

gates.name: payload_correct
gates.note: Rank-tagged payloads arrived where they belong. A summed checksum cannot tell a correct exchange from a permuted one.

gates.name: zero_mismatches
gates.note: No tolerance: this is an exact integer-valued comparison, not a floating-point one.

gates.name: uneven_splits_correct
gates.note: MoE routing produces uneven token counts per expert, including experts that receive nothing. Equal-split tests pass while this fails.

gates.name: has_zero_token_peers
gates.note: Guards the test itself: confirms the uneven case really did exercise a zero-token peer rather than silently degenerating to equal splits.

gates.name: communicator_churn_clean
gates.note: Repeated communicator create/destroy. Resource leaks show up here, not in a single-shot test.

gates.name: stayed_intra_node
gates.note: Guards the test itself: confirms this run really was the intra-node control.

gates.name: bandwidth_large_message_gbps
gates.note: PROVISIONAL -- recalibrate from a measured baseline. Reduced with `last` (largest message size), not `avg`: averaging across the sweep lets latency-bound small messages dominate. For reference the container's own suite asserts 37 GB/s for a far-pair intra-node point-to-point transfer at 64 MB; an 8-rank all-to-all mixes near and far pairs and shares links, so the per-rank figure is expected to be lower.
